messages:
amelia: Hey team — escalation from AcmeCorp. They reported repeated 429/503s for a batch job and two customer billing events went through twice. They say they're using python-sdk 1.3.2 (async client) and see duplicate charges when we retry on 429. Full details pasted below. Urgent — billing impact.

amelia: TL;DR: async retries sometimes resend a request without the original Idempotency-Key header after a token refresh, plus correlated retry bursts. Repro included.

amelia: Repro steps they sent:
```python
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(api_key="sk-...", retry_policy={"max_retries": 3})
async def run():
    resp = await client.create_charge(customer_id="cus_123", amount=100)
```
They run this in a few parallel workers and see two successful charges ~1s apart, with the first attempt returning 503 then retrying and succeeding.

chris: @amelia thanks — can you paste request/response headers and the SDK version exactly? 1.3.2 was the build that switched token refresh into the retry loop for async clients.

amelia: Headers: request 1 has Idempotency-Key: "ik-abc" then 503, retry attempt log shows subsequent request missing Idempotency-Key header. Responses show token refresh happened between attempts. Logs: 
```
[2025-10-12T11:02:01Z] request id=req-42 POST /v1/charges status=503 token_expired=true idempotency=ik-abc
[2025-10-12T11:02:01Z] token refresh start
[2025-10-12T11:02:02Z] retry attempt=1 POST /v1/charges status=200 idempotency=NONE
```

chris: This looks like a header mutation race during the async refresh path. We accidentally reuse the Request object and reapply headers after refresh, but the idempotency header is added in the per-call context and not copied back after the refresh. Also seeing our jitter seed was deterministic in 1.3.2 which can cause retry bursts across coroutines.

raj: I'm reproducing locally with the customer's snippet + aiohttp, can confirm missing Idempotency-Key on retry when refresh callback fires. Created a minimal repro:
```python
# repro_async_retry.py
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(api_key="sk-...", retry_policy={"max_retries": 2})
async def one():
    await client._send_with_refresh("/v1/charges", headers={"Idempotency-Key": "test-1"})
async def main():
    await asyncio.gather(*(one() for _ in range(5)))
asyncio.run(main())
```
Observing same behavior.

chris: Thanks @raj. Quick mitigation for customers: downgrade to 1.2.x (sync path unaffected) or pin 1.3.3-beta which contains a patch (not yet released). Workaround: set retry_policy={"max_retries": 0} and add server-side idempotency enforcement. We're preparing a hotfix.

amelia: Billing asked for timeline — @sylvia any guidance on refunds if duplicate charges are confirmed?

sylvia: If we confirm duplicates and they were caused by our SDK, issue a full refund immediately and CC legal for SLA credits. We need a billing ticket created with invoice ids.

chris: Root cause summary for the thread: async token refresh path mutated a shared request headers map; Idempotency-Key lived in the per-call context and wasn't merged back after refresh. Also deterministic jitter seeding in 1.3.2 made collisions more likely. Patch in PR #678 fixes both: deep-copy headers before refresh and use secure random seed for jitter.

chris: I'll open an internal hotfix build and post a link. ETA for hotfix build: ~2 hours. ETA for release and announcement: EOD after QA.

infra-bot: deploy check: CI job py-sdk-tests passed (run-4521) for hotfix branch.

raj: QA notes: test added to cover async refresh + idempotency header preserved; also added a stochastic stress test for jitter distribution. Passing locally.

amelia: I've notified the customer with a temporary mitigation and asked for request ids to reconcile billing. Keeping this thread updated.

chris: After release we'll publish an advisory: include repro script, affected versions (1.3.0-1.3.2), and recommended pin (1.2.x) or immediate upgrade to 1.3.3 when available.

sylvia: Please include a billing remediation template in the advisory so support can action refunds quickly.

amelia: Awesome. Marking as P1 until hotfix is deployed and at least 1 customer confirmed refunded.
